intro_screen_1_body: You have ◈60 and a roof you do not pay for. In five years someone will hand you a payslip and expect you to cope with it.
intro_screen_1_footnote: Nobody is going to test you on this. It just goes better if you know how it works.
intro_screen_2_body: ◈4,000 by the time you are nineteen. It does not come from a windfall or a lucky month. It comes out of the money you decide not to spend.
intro_screen_2_footnote: Money you do not spend is the only money you keep.
intro_screen_3_title: Plan it. Meet it. Close it.
intro_screen_3_body: You decide where the money goes before you know what the month holds. Then something happens, as it does. At the close you see what it cost.
intro_screen_3_footnote: Income lands when you start the month. The rest is up to you.
intro_privacy: Your progress is saved on this device with a random id. No name, no email, no tracking.
plan_subtitle: Put the money where you want it before the month gets a say.
plan_hint_body: The allowance stopped. This year, hours are the money.
plan_hint_note: Set them before the month starts.
plan_work_hours_hint: Every hour worked is an hour you do not get back.
plan_saving_note: the part that buys your future
event_blocked: Not enough free time — you cannot borrow hours.
event_cascade_debt: The cascade: {from} came out of the Save envelope, and {to} went onto Debt.
event_cascade_save: The cascade: {from} came out of the Save envelope.
resolve_over_note: You went past one of your envelopes this month. That is allowed — the cascade covered it — but the money came from somewhere.
stats_no_curve: The curve appears once a month has closed.
story_opening_debt: You started at 14 with {start} and finished at 19 with {final}, still owing {debt}.
story_opening_free: You started at 14 with {start} and finished at 19 with {final}, owing nothing.
story_adherence: You kept to the plan you set yourself in {months} of the 60 months.
story_band_ahead: You ended up past the goal you were aiming at, with the score to go with it.
story_band_treading: You ended up still moving — not ahead, and not sunk either.
story_band_behind: You ended up behind where you needed to be. Nothing is unrecoverable from here; that is the point of the five years.
story_band_note: your ending, from the money and the score
story_you_vs_you_note: Year one against year five. Nobody else's numbers.
story_what_next_body: The Fork comes round again in month 49. Studying and working end very differently.
story_saved: This Run is saved to your profile — playing again starts from month 1.
story_offline: This Run could not be saved. Reload to try the finish again.
settings_lead: The game keeps one thing about you: a random id and the Run it points at. Take it with you or delete it — neither needs an account.
settings_download_body: A JSON file holding everything the game keeps: the Run in progress, if there is one, and every finished Run kept for replay — the month, the money, the plan and the choices.
settings_delete_body: Removes every stored Run — the one in progress and any finished ones — and clears the id on this device. It cannot be undone: a fresh Run starts from month 1.
settings_delete_error: That did not go through. Nothing was deleted — try again.
privacy_heading: What the game knows about you.
privacy_lead: Short version: your progress, and nothing else.
flag_overdraft: Month {month}: you let the account go negative rather than wait.
flag_minimum_payment: Month {month}: you paid only the minimum, and the balance barely moved.
flag_card_issued: Month {month}: the card arrived, and with it a score to look after.
flag_fork_study: Month {month}: you chose to study, and the loan went on the sheet.
flag_fork_work: Month {month}: you chose to work, and paid a deposit on somewhere to live.
card_the_allowance_situation: Your parents sit you down. From now on you get ◈40 a month, and it is yours to get wrong. No top-ups.
card_the_allowance_choice_spend_label: Buy the thing you have been wanting
card_the_allowance_choice_spend_feedback: ◈40 in and ◈40 out in the same month. The first money you ever control is the easiest to spend, because nothing is asking for it yet.
card_the_allowance_choice_keep_label: Leave it where you cannot reach it
card_the_allowance_choice_keep_feedback: ◈40 that stayed put. Boring, invisible, and the only reason month one matters at all.
card_two_wants_situation: The game you have waited months for is out, and the headphones you actually need for school are on sale. You can afford one, today.
card_two_wants_choice_game_feedback: You picked the thing you wanted over the thing you needed. Nothing breaks today — the headphones not being there is next month’s problem.
card_two_wants_choice_headphones_feedbac: The boring one — and it was cheaper. That is not a sacrifice, it is a trade: ◈35 to stop a future problem before it starts.
card_odd_job_situation: Next door offers ◈30 to clear their garden this weekend. It is the whole weekend.
card_odd_job_choice_take_feedback: Fourteen hours for ◈30. That is about two an hour — and you will never forget it, which is exactly the point.
card_odd_job_choice_pass_feedback: Free time is real, and it is finite. You kept yours.
card_birthday_gift_situation: Your best friend’s birthday is on Friday. You have nothing for them yet.
card_birthday_gift_choice_buy_label: Buy the gift everyone is chipping in for
card_birthday_gift_choice_buy_feedback: ◈25 out of the Want envelope. That is what it is for — the only question is whether it was still there when Friday came.
card_birthday_gift_choice_make_feedback: Six hours instead of ◈25. Free is never free — you paid in the only currency you cannot borrow.
card_birthday_gift_choice_skip_feedback: You saved the money and spent something else. The game will not tell you that was wrong — you will find out.
card_phone_cracked_situation: It slipped out of your hand on the stairs. The screen is a spiderweb.
card_phone_cracked_choice_ack_feedback: A bill you did not plan for. This is what an emergency fund is for — and if it came out of the Save envelope or went onto Debt, that is the cascade doing its job.
card_insurance_offer_situation: Your phone is still in one piece — for now. Cover costs ◈6 a month.
card_insurance_offer_odds: About 1 in 3 of phones this age take a knock this year.
card_insurance_offer_choice_insure_feedb: ◈6 a month buys certainty. You will probably not claim — that is what insurance is: a small known amount to delete a big unknown one.
card_insurance_offer_choice_risk_feedbac: You kept the ◈6 and took the risk. Fine odds — until the phone lands on the stairs and you pay the whole repair yourself.
card_canteen_week_situation: The canteen takes about ◈5 a day. Packing lunch takes ten minutes each morning and costs about half as much.
card_canteen_week_choice_pack_feedback: Four hours a month for half the money. Cheap food is only cheap if the time was free, and yours mostly is.
card_canteen_week_choice_buy_feedback: ◈25 a month for not thinking about lunch. By summer that is a bike, and you will not remember a single sandwich.
card_dog_walking_situation: A woman two streets over needs her dog walked on school days. Three units a walk, every walk, in cash.
card_dog_walking_choice_take_feedback: Thirty a month for eight hours. Not much, and it is yours — the first money nobody gave you.
card_dog_walking_choice_pass_feedback: You kept your mornings. Somebody else got the thirty, and the dog got somebody else.
card_sell_games_situation: Twenty-three games, none of them played since last year. The trade-in app offers ◈45 for the lot.
card_sell_games_choice_sell_feedback: ◈45 for a shelf you had stopped seeing. Selling things you are finished with is the only tax-free income you have.
card_sell_games_choice_keep_feedback: You might. The drawer is a museum, and museums cost money to run — this one costs whatever the games could still be.
card_bus_pass_situation: Your bus pass is not in any pocket. A replacement is ◈30, or you walk forty minutes each way until it turns up.
card_bus_pass_choice_replace_feedback: Thirty, gone on a piece of plastic. The walk was the other price, and this month you decided the thirty was cheaper.
card_bus_pass_choice_walk_feedback: Twelve hours a month and sore shoes. The money would have been the cheaper price; you paid in the other currency.
card_grandma_windfall_situation: A card arrives late with ◈50 inside and a note that says do not spend it all at once.
card_grandma_windfall_choice_save_feedba: Thirty hidden before you found a use for it. Grandma has been right about this since before you were born.
card_grandma_windfall_choice_treat_feedb: Fifteen out, thirty-five still yours. Spending a windfall is not the mistake; spending it twice is.
card_trip_deposit_situation: The school trip costs ◈60, due in two months. The first ◈20 holds your place until then.
card_trip_deposit_choice_deposit_feedbac: Twenty holds the place, and now the other forty has a deadline and a reason.
card_trip_deposit_choice_wait_feedback: Waiting is free until the coach fills. Then it costs the whole trip.
card_hype_trainers_situation: The trainers everyone wants drop in four months at ◈90. Yours have a hole and still work.
card_hype_trainers_choice_save_feedback: Now the drop is something you are ready for. Saved-for things cost less than wanted things — always.
card_hype_trainers_choice_later_feedback: When they drop, ninety will feel like news. The version of you with the money already set aside is the version who gets them.
card_pocket_money_gone_situation: The ◈40 landed a week ago. There is ◈12 left and you honestly cannot say where the rest went.
card_pocket_money_gone_choice_track_feed: One hour to find the leak. Most of it went on small things you would have sworn were nothing.
card_pocket_money_gone_choice_shrug_feed: It is only twelve this week. Weeks are how months are made, and twenty-eight units went somewhere you cannot name.
card_fixer_bike_situation: Thirty for the bike with the loose wheel, an hour to fit the one you already have. Or ◈40 for the one that works outside the shop.
card_fixer_bike_choice_fix_feedback: Thirty and an hour, and it rides. Time and money are the same wallet; this one just spent the cheaper half.
card_fixer_bike_choice_ready_feedback: Forty for the version that needed nothing from you. Ten units was the fee for not getting your hands dirty.
card_phone_plan_situation: Your parents will keep paying for the phone, but only if you take the ◈15 a month plan yourself. It comes out either way.
card_phone_plan_choice_take_feedback: Fifteen a month, forever, before you have earned anything. This is the shape of being a grown-up: costs that do not care how your month went.
card_phone_plan_choice_cheaper_label: Shop around for a cheaper one
card_phone_plan_choice_cheaper_feedback: Three hours of comparing saved you a few units a month, every month, for as long as you keep it. That is the best-paid three hours in this entire game.
card_first_budget_situation: Last month you planned carefully and still ended up ◈12 short. Nothing dramatic happened — it was a lot of small things.
card_first_budget_choice_cover_label: Cover it from what you saved
card_first_budget_choice_cover_feedback: That is what the Save envelope is for, and using it was the right call. A buffer you are afraid to touch is not a buffer.
card_first_budget_choice_tighten_label: Spend an evening working out where it went
card_first_budget_choice_tighten_feedbac: Two hours to find ◈12 is a bad hourly rate. It is also how you find the six other things quietly doing the same, every month.
card_savings_goal_situation: A ◈300 bike you actually want, or a number with nothing attached to it. Both are saving. Only one of them you will keep doing.
card_savings_goal_choice_bike_feedback: Now the Save envelope has a face on it. Money with a job is far harder to raid than money with none.
card_savings_goal_choice_number_label: Keep it in your pocket for now
card_savings_goal_choice_number_feedback: Saving with no name attached is the one that quietly gets spent in month four. Give it a reason and it survives.
card_subscription_creep_situation: You add it up for the first time: streaming, storage, a game pass, two apps you forgot about. ◈28 a month.
card_subscription_creep_choice_cut_label: Cancel the ones you forgot about
card_subscription_creep_choice_cut_feedb: ◈14 a month back, forever, for ten minutes of admin. Nothing else in this game pays that well.
card_subscription_creep_choice_keep_feed: They are small. That is the whole trick. ◈28 a month is ◈336 a year, and you will never see it leave.
card_concert_tickets_situation: Your friends are going tonight. Tickets are ◈35 and you have ◈60 saved toward the bike.
card_concert_tickets_choice_go_feedback: The money came out of the Save envelope, which is exactly where it should come from if you have decided this is worth it. You did decide, right?
card_concert_tickets_choice_stay_feedbac: You kept the ◈35 and missed the night. There is no refund for that either — both options cost something.
card_phone_bill_spike_situation: The first bill arrives at ◈40. The plan said ◈15. The difference is data you apparently used without noticing.
card_phone_bill_spike_choice_pay_label: Pay it and watch the usage
card_phone_bill_spike_choice_pay_feedbac: ◈25 for finding out that the plan and the bill are different documents. Watching the usage is part of the month now.
card_phone_bill_spike_choice_challenge_f: Twenty minutes of hold music and the charge was halved. Complaining, done properly, has an hourly rate.
card_no_spend_week_situation: A zero-spend week: nothing that is not transport or food. Your friends think it is a joke.
card_no_spend_week_choice_do_feedback: Two hours of planning and a week that went where you said. A sense of control is hard to buy and easy to build.
card_no_spend_week_choice_skip_feedback: Fifteen on the usual small things. Nothing dramatic, which is exactly how the envelope empties.
card_gift_fund_situation: Three birthdays this month and presents will run about ◈30. Payday is not soon.
card_gift_fund_choice_plan_feedback: A list, a cap, and gifts nobody squinted at. Planning made the same three birthdays half the price.
card_gift_fund_choice_wing_feedback: Thirty, and two of the presents were chosen in a panic at the till. Panic is the most expensive shop.
card_savings_milestone_situation: The savings account says ◈200 for the first time. Nothing happened except you not spending it, sixteen times.
card_savings_milestone_choice_add_feedba: Two hundred and twenty. The number is not the point; the sixteen decisions behind it are.
card_savings_milestone_choice_celebrate_: Ten spent on the milestone and one hundred ninety still working. Celebrating cheaply is how the streak survives.
card_data_plan_shrink_situation: The plan is ◈15 a month for more data than you have ever used. The smaller one is ◈9 and you will feel it on trips.
card_data_plan_shrink_choice_shrink_feed: Six a month, forever, for ten minutes of admin. The smaller plan stings twice a year and pays every month.
card_data_plan_shrink_choice_stay_feedba: Comfort costs six a month. That is the trade: a little convenience now, a larger number by the end of school.
card_till_impulse_situation: Every shop puts the same small things by the till. You have walked past them four times this week and bought them twice.
card_till_impulse_choice_rule_feedback: One hour to decide what the till aisle is allowed to cost. Rules beat willpower, because willpower has homework.
card_till_impulse_choice_buy_feedback: Twelve this week. The till aisle is not an accident; it is the most profitable square metre in the shop.
card_first_payslip_situation: The café takes you on, ten an hour. Your first shift is Saturday. Nobody has explained how many you will want.
card_first_payslip_choice_enthusiastic_f: ◈80 and no weekend. Nothing is free, but look at what an hour is actually worth — now you know the exchange rate.
card_first_payslip_choice_measured_feedb: ◈50 and you still have a life. Working out how much time you are willing to sell is the whole negotiation.
card_interest_first_situation: Your savings went up this month and you did not put anything in. It was ◈0.12, and it was not there before.
card_interest_first_choice_more_feedback: More in means more interest means more in. It is the only thing in this game that works while you sleep.
card_interest_first_choice_nothing_label: Leave it — twelve units is nothing
card_interest_first_choice_nothing_feedb: ◈0.12 is nothing. ◈0.12 every month for forty years is not, and that is the bit nobody can see yet.
card_extra_shift_situation: Your manager is short-staffed on Saturday and asks if you can cover. It is the same day as the match.
card_extra_shift_choice_take_feedback: Eight hours at ten an hour, and it landed as ◈80. Money you earn is hours you do not get back — that is the trade, every time.
card_extra_shift_choice_pass_feedback: You kept the day. Nothing wrong with that — but the ◈80 does not exist, and next month’s plan has to live without it.
card_bnpl_trainers_situation: The trainers are ◈120. The shop offers four monthly payments of ◈30, interest-free.
card_bnpl_trainers_choice_now_feedback: Paid and done. Painful in one month, and the whole thing is behind you.
card_bnpl_trainers_choice_bnpl_feedback: Four payments of ◈30 — and the part nobody says out loud: it built you no credit score. Paying it perfectly changes nothing about your file.
card_bnpl_trainers_choice_skip_feedback: Not this month. Nothing was lost.
card_lend_to_friend_situation: Your mate needs ◈40 until next week. You have it. You have also watched them not pay people back.
card_lend_to_friend_choice_lend_feedback: It came out of the Save envelope. If it comes back, nothing happened. If it does not, you paid ◈40 to find something out.
card_lend_to_friend_choice_no_feedback: You kept the money and the awkwardness. Saying no to money you cannot spare is a skill, and it never feels good.
card_lend_returns_situation: Three weeks later your mate slides ◈20 across the table. The other twenty is definitely next week, and the group chat is already planning the next night out.
card_lend_returns_choice_take_feedback: Half the money back without a conversation. The other half is now a question you will have to ask, and you both know it.
card_lend_returns_choice_chase_feedback: Forty recovered, and two hours of a friendship held at arm’s length. The money came back; the borrowing probably will not.
card_evening_course_situation: The college runs an evening coding course — three months, two evenings a week, ◈90 up front. Past students say the certificate is the part that gets you looked at.
card_evening_course_choice_enrol_feedbac: ◈90 up front and two evenings a week until spring. The money was never the expensive half.
card_evening_course_choice_skip_feedback: The certificate stays on the college noticeboard, and so does the version of you that has one.
card_course_pays_off_situation: Last class done. The certificate sits in a drawer for a week, and then Priya offers you the closing shift — the one that pays a little more if you can hold the till and the book.
card_course_pays_off_choice_ask_feedback: You said the number out loud and got ◈60 of better shifts. The certificate opened the door; asking walked through it.
card_course_pays_off_choice_quiet_feedba: Thirty, and no conversation. The other thirty stayed in somebody else’s budget.
card_overtime_offer_situation: Ravi is ill and the café needs Friday and Saturday covered. It is ◈45 and your entire weekend.
card_overtime_offer_choice_take_feedback: Forty-five for the weekend. When you spend time like money, you start seeing what it costs.
card_overtime_offer_choice_pass_feedback: You kept the weekend. Some weekends are worth forty-five; this one gets to be whatever you make it.
card_inflated_prices_situation: The meal deal went up again. Same sandwich, ten per cent more, and it is the fourth thing this year that quietly did.
card_inflated_prices_choice_replan_feedb: Two hours to move the lines. Prices only cost what they cost — quietly not noticing is the expensive part.
card_inflated_prices_choice_carry_feedba: Twelve this month. Prices rarely come back down, so absorbing it once means absorbing it every month.
card_payday_timing_situation: The wage hits the account on Friday. By Sunday the weekend has taken a third of it, and the month is still twenty-eight days long.
card_payday_timing_choice_move_feedback: One hour on Friday to decide what the weekend may spend. The same wage, a different month.
card_payday_timing_choice_weekend_feedba: Twenty-five on the weekend and the rest of the month does the adjusting. Wages come monthly; weekends come weekly.
card_shift_clash_situation: The café offers you every Saturday for the next two months. Your friends have started planning things that happen on Saturdays.
card_shift_clash_choice_work_feedback: Sixty for eight weekends. Real money and a real cost, and only one of them shows on a statement.
card_shift_clash_choice_life_feedback: Fifteen for the two weekends and the version of you who is not always at work. Both lines are real.
card_meal_deal_situation: The meal deal is six: sandwich, drink, snack. The sandwich alone is four. The drink is one you would not have bought.
card_meal_deal_choice_alone_feedback: Four for the thing you came in for. The deal saves money on a bigger basket than you meant to buy.
card_meal_deal_choice_deal_feedback: Six and a free drink that was not free. Bundles win when you wanted all of it, and only then.
card_phone_repair_situation: The phone is cracked again. Repair is sixty; a refurbished one is a hundred and fifty, and yours has two good years left.
card_phone_repair_choice_repair_feedback: Sixty to keep something that works. Repair is almost always cheaper than replace, and almost never feels like it.
card_phone_repair_choice_replace_feedbac: One hundred fifty for new glass and a fresh battery. The old one was not broken enough to justify it.
card_cut_a_shift_situation: You are on the rota five evenings a week and the schoolwork is starting to show it. A shift is worth about thirty.
card_cut_a_shift_choice_cut_feedback: Thirty given up to get the evenings back. That is the exchange rate, and now you have priced it.
card_cut_a_shift_choice_keep_feedback: Thirty for eight more hours. Both choices are a trade; only one of them leaves room for homework.
card_trial_renewal_situation: The app you signed up to in the summer is about to bill you nine a month. You have opened it twice since June.
card_trial_renewal_choice_cancel_feedbac: Ten minutes and nine a month stays yours. The trial was designed for exactly this moment to be easy to skip.
card_trial_renewal_choice_renew_feedback: Nine for something you might use. Subscriptions are the only bill you have to remember to stop.
card_quarterly_interest_situation: The statement has a new line: interest paid. Nine units have appeared that nobody worked for.
card_quarterly_interest_choice_leave_fee: Ten more where the nine came from. Compounding is a snowball with a very long hill, and you just started it.
card_quarterly_interest_choice_skim_feed: Nine units out and the snowball starts again. Withdrawing interest feels like free money; it is the opposite.
card_bnpl_offer_situation: At seventeen the shop app now offers you a limit of ◈300. No card, no paperwork, no explanation of what happens if you do not pay.
card_bnpl_offer_choice_use_feedback: It went through in one tap. That is the design. Something that takes one tap to start and months to finish is not convenience.
card_bnpl_offer_choice_leave_feedback: You left the limit untouched. It will still be there next month, and the things you would have bought will not matter by then.
card_minimum_payment_situation: Your card statement arrives. You owe ◈300. The minimum payment is ◈15, and the full payment is — well, ◈300.
card_minimum_payment_choice_full_feedbac: Full payment, no interest, score up. It hurt once and then it was over. This is the only version of a card that is not a trap.
card_minimum_payment_choice_minimum_feed: ◈15 comes off the balance and almost all of it was interest. At this rate the trainers cost you far more than ◈300.
card_credit_limit_rise_situation: Your limit goes from ◈300 to ◈800. Nothing about your income changed. A friend points out you could finally afford the trip.
card_credit_limit_rise_choice_accept_lab: Put the trip on the card
card_credit_limit_rise_choice_accept_fee: The trip was real and so is the balance. More room to spend is more rope — the limit was never your money.
card_credit_limit_rise_choice_ignore_fee: A credit limit is a permission slip, not a raise. Knowing the difference is most of what this stage teaches.
card_overdraft_situation: Five days until you are paid and you are ◈40 short. Three friends are going out tonight.
card_overdraft_choice_dip_feedback: The bank covers it and charges you for the favour, and the score notices. Borrowing ◈40 at a rate you never agreed to.
card_overdraft_choice_wait_feedback: You sat five days out. Boring, free, and it did nothing to your file. Most of the time this is the whole answer.
card_rent_share_situation: Friends want you in a shared flat. Your share is ◈650, plus a deposit, plus the things nobody lists when they quote a rent.
card_rent_share_choice_commit_feedback: Rent is the cost that does not flinch. Everything else in your month bends around this number, so it has to be right.
card_rent_share_choice_wait_feedback: You stayed put. It costs nothing, buys time, and is the right call exactly as often as it is the easy one.
card_late_fee_situation: The payment came out on a day the account was empty. The bank wants ◈25 for the privilege.
card_late_fee_choice_pay_feedback: Twenty-five, and the account is square. Fees pay for the mistake; leaving them unpaid pays for it every month.
card_late_fee_choice_leave_feedback: It sits there, quietly growing a report card. Unpaid costs become a record, and records follow you.
card_instalment_week_situation: The payment goes out this week and the week is already thin. You said the same thing last month.
card_instalment_week_choice_tighten_feed: Two hours of cooking instead of a week of buying. The instalment was decided months ago; the week was decided today.
card_instalment_week_choice_dip_feedback: Thirty out of savings to feed a decision you made months ago. That is what the four payments actually cost.
card_score_check_situation: The banking app has a number for you now: 640. It went down five points and nothing on screen says why.
card_score_check_choice_read_feedback: Five points, and a page explaining every rule that moves them. People who know the rules pay less for the same money.
card_score_check_choice_close_feedback: The number is still there, still moving, still deciding what the next loan costs. Not looking is free until it is not.
card_score_goal_situation: The phone contract needs a credit check. No score means a deposit of a hundred, or buying a handset outright today.
card_score_goal_choice_wait_feedback: Two hours to learn which payments move the number. The deposit exists because nobody can see you yet.
card_score_goal_choice_outright_feedback: One hundred twenty to skip a queue nobody wants to be in. Owning it outright is never the wrong answer.
card_refuse_the_limit_situation: The shop app now lets you spread four hundred in four payments. It suggests this at the checkout now, above the button.
card_refuse_the_limit_choice_stick_label: Stick to what you can repay
card_refuse_the_limit_choice_stick_feedb: The basket went down to what the account could cover. The one-tap button is doing arithmetic you are not.
card_refuse_the_limit_choice_basket_feed: Eighty spread over four payments, decided in a second. The decision was made by whoever put the button there.
card_credit_check_free_situation: The bank lets you see your score for free, with a page explaining every line. It takes about an evening.
card_credit_check_free_choice_read_feedb: Two hours to find the late payment you had forgotten and the fix that takes one phone call. Cheapest maintenance there is.
card_credit_check_free_choice_skip_feedb: Skipped. The number keeps moving either way, and the people who watch it pay less for the same borrowings.
card_bnpl_pressure_situation: The group is buying the same trainers in four payments. Nobody is talking about what the third payment feels like in a thin month.
card_bnpl_pressure_choice_save_feedback: Forty now, the rest when the money exists. The trainers arrive later and nobody is owed anything.
card_bnpl_pressure_choice_split_feedback: Four payments, and the first one is not the problem. The third one lands in the month you cannot see yet.
card_payday_drain_situation: The wage landed Friday and the account is already thin. Nothing big happened; a lot of small things did.
card_payday_drain_choice_map_feedback: Three hours to put the month on a line. You have watched the same Friday twice a month for a year.
card_payday_drain_choice_wait_feedback: Twenty that went somewhere unplanned, which is a fine definition of drift. Wages land in spikes; lives cost in drips.
card_the_fork_situation: That is it — school done. Study, or start working? This one you do not get back.
card_the_fork_choice_study_label: Study — part-time work, and a 3,000 loan
card_the_fork_choice_study_feedback: You took the loan. It is on the balance sheet from today, which is the point: deferred debt is still debt, and your net worth starts this year flat rather than rich.
card_the_fork_choice_work_label: Work — full time, and a flat of your own
card_the_fork_choice_work_feedback: Full-time wage, and rent the moment you move — starting with the deposit. This is why saving in year one mattered.
card_first_taxed_payslip_situation: Your first full payslip shows a number you agreed to and a smaller number arriving. Between them sits a line called withholding.
card_first_taxed_payslip_choice_read_fee: Twenty per cent, taken before you ever see it. Annoying — and the reason it hurts less than a bill you have to pay yourself.
card_first_taxed_payslip_choice_ignore_f: You skipped it. Most people do. The deduction happens whether or not you looked, and it is worth two minutes once a month.
card_the_fund_situation: Your savings keep pace with rising prices and barely beat them. There is a fund that has averaged seven per cent a year, and lost a quarter in a bad one.
card_the_fund_choice_open_feedback: Four hundred in. You now own something that moves — which is the price of it being able to move upward.
card_the_fund_choice_wait_feedback: You stayed in savings: safe, liquid, and losing to prices by a hair. There is no wrong answer here, only a trade.
card_the_crash_situation: Everything in the fund is down a quarter in two months. Everyone on the internet has an opinion and all of them are panicking.
card_the_crash_choice_buy_label: Put more in while it is cheap
card_the_crash_choice_buy_feedback: Buying when everyone is selling is the hardest version of this and historically the best-paying one. You will not feel clever this month.
card_the_crash_choice_hold_feedback: You held. The loss only becomes real if you sell, and the recovery always happens without you if you do. This is the whole lesson.
card_the_crash_choice_sell_feedback: You sold at the bottom, which is when the story feels most convincing. The fall was temporary; locking it in was your decision.
card_scam_opportunity_situation: A message from someone who knows a friend of yours. ◈200 becomes ◈600 in six weeks, guaranteed, but you have to move today.
card_scam_opportunity_choice_in_feedback: Guaranteed, urgent, and paid by transfer. Those three words have never once been true together. The ◈200 is gone and nobody to ask.
card_scam_opportunity_choice_check_feedb: Urgency is the tell. Real investments survive being thought about overnight, and everything that cannot is selling you something else.
card_scam_opportunity_choice_block_feedb: Gone. They will try again with a different story, because it works on someone.
card_app_tip_situation: Danny has an app. His cousin turned ◈40 into ◈52 last month and has screenshots. The button says invest and the countdown says nine minutes.
card_app_tip_choice_in_feedback: Fifty into an app with a cartoon rocket and a countdown. Every part of that sentence was a tell.
card_app_tip_choice_out_label: Ask where the returns come from
card_app_tip_choice_out_feedback: He did not know, and the group chat moved on. Nobody ever explains where guaranteed money comes from, because there is nowhere.
card_app_vanishes_situation: The app is gone from the store. Danny’s cousin is typing in capitals. Yesterday your ◈50 showed as ◈68, and today there is no screen at all.
card_app_vanishes_choice_report_feedback: The fraud line says the money left by choice and cannot be clawed back. The two hours still put a number on a list that gets someone caught.
card_app_vanishes_choice_chalk_feedback: Fifty to learn that guaranteed money is a story people tell. That is a cheap version of a lesson that usually costs more.
card_the_limit_letter_situation: The card company has raised your limit to ◈500 and would like you to know it is there for you.
card_the_limit_letter_choice_ignore_feed: Five hundred available, zero used. A number going up is not money arriving, however much it looks like it.
card_the_limit_letter_choice_use_feedbac: Sixty on the card is sixty decided now and repaid later. The ceiling gets closer every time you touch it.
card_cash_in_hand_situation: A builder pays you ◈120 in notes for clearing a site. Nothing is written down anywhere.
card_cash_in_hand_choice_declare_feedbac: Ninety after the deduction and a record that the work was real. Boring, and the version you can prove.
card_cash_in_hand_choice_quiet_feedback: One hundred twenty, untouched. Nothing happens until something else does and there is no record you were ever there.
card_refund_text_situation: A text says the tax office owes you ◈240. The link asks for your bank details, and the deadline is today.
card_refund_text_choice_click_feedback: A refund you never claimed, a link, and a deadline. The ◈240 was the hook; the ◈120 was the price.
card_refund_text_choice_check_feedback: One hour on the real tax site and the text is gone. Refunds arrive in writing, from numbers you never had to ask about.
card_boring_fund_situation: A friend of a friend turned ◈300 into ◈2,000 in a month. He is posting the screenshots again.
card_boring_fund_choice_fund_label: Put it in the boring fund
card_boring_fund_choice_fund_feedback: Fifty into seven per cent and a graph that moves too slowly to post. Slow is not a bug; it is the whole offer.
card_boring_fund_choice_chase_label: Put thirty in the same thing
card_boring_fund_choice_chase_feedback: Thirty in after the screenshot, which is when the story is most expensive. You bought at the part he was selling.
card_first_statement_situation: One page, two numbers that matter: the full balance, or the minimum that keeps everything going.
card_first_statement_choice_clear_feedba: Paid in full before the interest existed. No fee, no letter next month, and the score moves the right way.
card_first_statement_choice_minimum_feed: Ten now and a balance that ignores you. The minimum is affordable forever, which is exactly the business model.
card_payslip_error_situation: The payslip says sixty-two hours. You worked seventy. The difference is about ◈45 before the deduction line even sees it.
card_payslip_error_choice_query_feedback: Three hours of rota printouts and the missing hours arrived next pay. Payroll errs in both directions, and only one of them fixes itself.
card_payslip_error_choice_drop_feedback: Forty-five left on the table because chasing it felt awkward. That is the most expensive kind of awkward there is.
card_side_work_situation: A mate’s market stall needs a hand on weekends. Forty a day, cash, and both days are possible.
card_side_work_choice_take_feedback: Eighty for the weekend. Extra money always costs something; the arithmetic only starts with the number.
card_side_work_choice_one_feedback: Forty and one day left. Half the money, half the cost, and the option to do it again next week.
card_grown_up_cover_situation: You now own enough that losing it would matter. Cover on everything you own is ◈12 a month.
card_grown_up_cover_odds: Roughly 1 in 12 renters claim in a given year.
card_grown_up_cover_choice_insure_feedba: Twelve a month against losing everything at once. Insurance is not for the likely month, it is for the one you could not survive.
card_grown_up_cover_choice_risk_feedback: You kept the ◈12. Most years that is the right trade, and the year it is not, it is very much not.
card_rent_due_situation: Rent leaves on the first. It is more than half of everything you bring in, and it does not care what the rest of the month looked like.
card_rent_due_choice_pay_label: Pay it and plan around it
card_rent_due_choice_pay_feedback: Paid first, everything else second. Planning backwards from the biggest fixed cost is the only version that survives.
card_rent_due_choice_delay_label: Let it go late this once
card_rent_due_choice_delay_feedback: Once becomes the pattern faster than anyone expects, and the fee is the smallest part of what it costs you.
card_graduate_job_situation: Full-time, twelve and a half an hour, and the training nobody offers you in person. It is more than you have ever earned.
card_graduate_job_choice_take_feedback: First real job. The wage is the small part — what you learn to do next is the bit that gets compounded.
card_graduate_job_choice_push_feedback: You asked. Two hours of preparation for a number you keep for years is the highest-paid work you will ever do.
card_commute_costs_situation: The monthly travel pass is ◈90. Walking is an hour each way, and the shifts already finish late.
card_commute_costs_choice_pass_feedback: Ninety to arrive with a life left. The pass looks like the expensive option until you price the other one.
card_commute_costs_choice_walk_feedback: Twelve hours a month on your own feet. The job pays the wage; getting to it charges rent.
card_shift_swap_situation: The late shift pays two an hour more and finishes after the last bus. Nobody else wants it.
card_shift_swap_choice_late_feedback: Sixty for the shifts nobody wanted. Every workplace pays for the hours everyone else is asleep.
card_shift_swap_choice_early_feedback: You kept the evenings and left the premium on the table. A fair trade, as long as it was a trade.
card_ask_for_rise_situation: You have covered eleven shifts in a row and the wage has not moved. The manager is in the office.
card_ask_for_rise_choice_ask_feedback: Two hours of preparation and forty you keep every month after. Asking is the highest-paid work there is.
card_ask_for_rise_choice_wait_feedback: You will be noticed eventually, when someone else asks and gets it. The wage does not move by itself.
card_housemate_leaves_situation: A flatmate is moving out. Until someone else signs, the rent is a hundred a month more than the plan.
card_housemate_leaves_choice_cover_feedb: A hundred out of what you had put aside. This is what the buffer was for, and it will not last many months.
card_housemate_leaves_choice_advertise_f: Six hours of viewings and awkward questions. Rooms fill; the gap only shrinks when someone does this.
card_boots_situation: The site needs steel-toe boots. New is ◈70; a barely-used pair is ◈30 if you can find the size.
card_boots_choice_new_feedback: Seventy and the right size straight away. The job pays for the boots eventually, and it is not the job paying today.
card_boots_choice_used_feedback: Thirty and four hours of hunting. Same steel, cheaper leather, and you paid the difference in time.
card_student_budget_situation: The loan lands, and it feels like income. It is not income. It is next year’s money arriving early, with your name on it.
card_student_budget_choice_spread_label: Put the term’s rent aside now
card_student_budget_choice_spread_feedba: Spread across the term, it becomes a wage. Spent in the first month, it becomes debt you are still paying at twenty-five.
card_student_budget_choice_celebrate_fee: The first month of a loan always feels like money. The fourth month is where the whole thing is decided.
card_textbook_week_situation: Three books on the list, ◈120 new. Second-hand copies are about ◈15 each, if you can find them.
card_textbook_week_choice_hunt_feedback: Forty-five and an afternoon of messages. The knowledge is identical; the cover is cheaper.
card_textbook_week_choice_new_feedback: One hundred twenty for the convenience of starting today. The lecture is the same; the receipt is not.
card_exam_crunch_situation: Exams in a fortnight and the café would give you every shift you asked for.
card_exam_crunch_choice_revise_feedback: Eight hours in the quiet room. The shifts will be there in three weeks; the exam will not.
card_exam_crunch_choice_shifts_feedback: Fifty for a fortnight you will not get back before the exam. That is the trade: paid now, paid for later.
card_internship_lead_situation: A lab wants a summer helper — real work, a reference at the end, and two days a week all summer.
card_internship_lead_choice_take_feedbac: A hundred for the summer and a line on the CV that outlives every shift you did not take.
card_internship_lead_choice_focus_feedba: You kept the summer for the term and the term for yourself. Nothing wasted, nothing gained, and doors do not stay open.
card_student_discount_situation: A railcard is ◈30 and takes a third off every train home for a year. You go home about once a month.
card_student_discount_choice_buy_feedbac: Thirty up front against twelve cheaper trips. Spending to save wins whenever the trips actually happen.
card_student_discount_choice_fare_feedba: Fifteen this trip and fifteen next. Paying as you go keeps the choice open and the total higher.
card_study_group_coffee_title: The group meets at a café
card_study_group_coffee_situation: The study group meets three times a week at a café, and everyone buys something. The cheapest thing is four.
card_study_group_coffee_choice_round_fee: Twenty-four a month to belong to the group. That is not a scam — it is a cost, and now it is on the sheet.
card_study_group_coffee_choice_host_feed: Three hours tidying and a kettle. Belonging is still paid for; only the currency changed.
